application.name: cat(a)log
application.summary: Shared memory of your animals: where each lives, what happened, who did what.
application.desc: cat(a)log is the shared memory of a group of people who care for cats — or for any pets. It answers, at any time and for every animal: who is this, where does it live right now, what has happened to it, and who did what, when. It is built for how animal care actually works. Cats move: from the shelter to a foster home, from the foster home to an adopter, out of a garden and onto the street, back again. Several people keep the record: you, the person who covers your weekends, the neighbour who feeds the colony. Nobody has a server, and nothing must get lost. THE RECORD • Every animal has a place. Cats live in clowders — your home, a foster home, an adopter's flat, the barn behind the station. Moving one is a dated event, so the record knows where Miezi was in May and who has her now. An animal without a place is a stray, and the app treats it as one. • Every fact has a date and a name. Neutered, vaccinated, weighed, moved, renamed: the app stores when it happened and who wrote it down, not just the current value. A cat's page reads like a diary. Nothing is ever overwritten; a mistake is corrected with a new entry, and the correction is visible too. • Weight and every other number get a graph. Weight is built in, in your units — kilograms or pounds, as your region says — and any number you log, a temperature or a dose, is drawn over time: week, month, year, the change since last time, vet visits marked along the way. • Several people, one record, no server. Each helper carries the whole catalog on their own device. Phones sync directly and encrypted over Wi-Fi, through a folder you already share (Nextcloud, Syncthing, a USB stick), or as a file through any messenger. If two people changed the same thing at once, both versions are shown and you decide. • One cat is one cat. Chip numbers and registry numbers (TASSO and others, opened with one tap) identify an animal. Two entries that are the same cat are merged, and both histories survive. A stray seen inside the search area of a missing cat is offered as a possible match. WHAT THAT MEANS DAY TO DAY • Fostering a litter: which of the ten identical kittens is already neutered, which one went to the family in the next town, and when. One vet appointment for the whole litter — tick the cats that come along, and afterwards note who was treated. • Feeding a colony: a new face at the feeding spot gets a photo and a position with one tap; when it turns up two streets away, the map draws its trail. Over months, the record shows who belongs to the colony and who was passing through. • A cat is missing: photograph the poster you hang up, or one somebody else hung up. The app reads the poster, marks the spot, and draws the 500 m area where the cat probably roams. The next sighting inside that area lands on the right cat. • Your own pets: switch a catalog to pets and it speaks of pets and households — dog, rabbit, horse, whatever lives with you, each with its own breeds. Chip number, vaccinations, vet visits, medication, weight — and appointments in an agenda your phone's calendar can mirror. ALSO • Your own fields — "flea treatment", "favourite food", a body temperature in °C or °F — behave like the built-in ones, history and graph included. • Photos: crop one kitten out of a group picture, or circle it when they are too tangled to crop. • A printable page per animal with photo and chip code, for the vet or the adopter. • Runs offline. Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux. • 38 languages, right-to-left included. • Free, open source (Apache-2.0 / MIT), no ads, no account, no tracking. Your data stays on your devices, in a format you can read and export.

application.name: chaos-alert
application.summary: Bedtime nag, a word to remember, and an alarm that never sounds the same
application.desc:
Your alarm always sounds the same, so you sleep right through it. And "just ten more minutes" on the sofa turns into midnight again. chaos-alert nags you to bed when it's time, gives you one word to remember, and wakes you with a sound you never hear coming. To turn the alarm off, you pick last night's word from four. A wrong pick only snoozes it, and the app keeps count of how well you remembered. What it does
  • Bedtime nag — at bedtime a quiet full-screen popup asks: Are you in bed? Bedtime follows from tomorrow's first alarm and how much sleep you want. Not yet? Snooze 10 minutes, or 30 min, 1 h, 2 h when you're out. Fell asleep without answering? The popup's time counts as your bedtime and nothing wakes you. Each popup also makes its case first, with one of 300 lines about sleep, dreams, puffy eyes, the Matrix and fairy tales.
  • In bed early — the main screen offers "I'm in bed" in the three hours before bedtime.
  • A word for the night — one less common English word, shown once.
  • The chaos alarm — every ring picks something random: an alarm sound, a notification sound or a song from your music. Quiet at first, louder after 10 seconds, a new surprise after every snooze.
  • The quiz — four words, one of them last night's. Tap to mark, then OK. A wrong word snoozes the alarm and drops out of the next try; the page after the right one shows how many tries it took, your streak and your last 30 nights. Five failures in a row bring a gentle hint.
  • I'm awake — up before the alarm? In the hour before it, a button and a silent notification take you to the quiz; the right word turns off that morning's alarms.
  • Alarms — repeating on weekdays or once on a date; reminder alarms that shouldn't move your bedtime simply get their wake-up switch turned off.
  • Vacations — enter the dates once; repeating alarms and the nag stay quiet, one-time alarms still ring.
  • Time in bed — a week or a month of bars, coloured by how the quiz went, with your average time in bed and average bedtime.
Everything stays on your phone: no account, no internet permission, no tracking. Free and open source.

application.name: Old Brain Fix
application.summary: Notes, reminders and routines with exact alarms. No account, no server.
application.desc: Old Brain Fix is a note and reminder app for Android. A desktop app for Linux, Windows and macOS uses the same data. There is no account and no server; all data is stored on the user's own devices. Capture • Text, photo and voice Notes, opened from the + button, home-screen widgets, Quick Settings tiles, app shortcuts, or a hardware button where the phone allows assigning one. • Content shared from other apps is saved as a Note. • Each Note records the time of capture. Optional: the location (shown as a Named Place such as "Home" when one matches), the current calendar event and the connected Bluetooth device. • Voice Notes are transcribed on the device with Whisper (English and German). The speech model (148 MB) is downloaded once, on request. • Text in photos and screenshots is recognised on the device with ocrs. Recognition covers unaccented Latin letters only. • Transcripts and recognised text are included in search. Organising • New Notes are kept in Unsorted. A notification (Nudge) reports Unsorted Notes at a set interval; Quiet Hours suppress it at night. • Notes are filed into Areas and Topics (two levels), each with a colour and an icon. A starter set of Areas is offered at first start. • Notes can be edited, amended and merged. Deleted items stay in the trash for 30 days. Routines and Reminders • Any Note can have Reminders (one time) and Routines (repeating by a recurrence rule, several times a day if needed). • Alarms ring at the exact minute, also on the lock screen, and are restored after a restart. This requires the "Alarms & reminders" permission. • An alarm that is neither marked Done nor snoozed rings again at a set interval (Re-nag, default 10 minutes). Optionally, after a set number of repeats it is shown as a full-screen alarm with sound. • The Agenda lists today's Routines and Reminders, missed ones and the number of Unsorted Notes. It is also available as a home-screen widget. • Each Routine has a history with streak and adherence. • Routines and Reminders can be written to a device calendar or exported as an ICS file. Sync and sharing • Phone and desktop sync directly over the local network (TLS, paired by QR code or typed code), through a shared folder such as Syncthing or Nextcloud (end-to-end encrypted), or through an encrypted file sent with any app. • A single Area can be shared with another person. Other Areas are not shared. • Your Profile unites all of your Devices. Your name, a unique code and an optional picture show on the Notes you share with others. • A Note can be sent to another person as a file, together with its Routines and Reminders. The receiver can accept or decline it. Privacy and security • No account, no server, no analytics, no advertising. • The app uses the network only for sync and for the speech model download. • Optional App Lock (PIN, fingerprint) and Area Locks. Capture and alarms keep working while locked. • Encrypted Backups (Argon2id, XChaCha20-Poly1305) into a chosen folder, optionally weekly, with a printable Recovery Sheet. Optionally, Android's backup to Google stores the encrypted Backup file and nothing else. Other • English and German. Light and dark theme. • Free and open source, licensed under Apache-2.0 or MIT.
